title: Brazil’s Pix transition is rapid but incomplete: actual cash displacement coexists with knowledge and connectivity barriers
source_unit: Banco Central do Brasil, second edition of O brasileiro e os hábitos de uso de meios de pagamento, data collected October–November 2023
geography: Brazil; national adult consumer survey, merchant survey, and one-week payment diaries, with payment-method, preference, income-receipt, and barrier dimensions

denominator.unit: payment diaries in the 2023 study; 11,023 recorded payments across participating individuals

cash_payment_share_2019.unit: percent of diary-recorded payments made with cash in 2019

cash_payment_share_2023.unit: percent of diary-recorded payments made with cash in 2023

cash_decline.unit: percentage-point decline in cash share of recorded payments from 2019 to 2023, calculated from published shares

pix_payment_share_2023.unit: percent of diary-recorded payments made with Pix in 2023

mechanism.value: Pix is not only an infrastructure rollout: it is displacing cash in observed consumer transactions, changing the visibility, speed, and routing of everyday consumption while leaving cash as a major residual instrument

observations.method: BCB comparison of one-week payment diaries from the 2019 and 2023 editions; the 2023 release reports 1,228 diaries and 11,023 recorded transactions.
observations.uncertainty: The two diary samples and field periods may differ; payment shares do not measure transaction value, merchant acceptance, cash withdrawals, household welfare, or causal effects of Pix.
observations.subgroup: Brazilian consumers participating in the 2019 and 2023 payment-diary studies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cash may remain important for privacy, offline resilience, informal commerce, or specific merchant contexts; Pix use does not imply complete replacement of cash or equal access.

observations.period: 2023; stated preference, awareness, and non-use barriers

denominator.unit: individuals in the quantitative consumer survey; separate 600-establishment survey and 1,228 payment diaries were also fielded

pix_preference.unit: percent of people naming Pix among their two most preferred payment methods

cash_preference.unit: percent naming cash among their two most preferred payment methods

pix_nonuse_last_12_months.unit: percent of interviewees who did not use Pix in the preceding 12 months

nonuser_lack_of_knowledge.unit: percent of Pix nonusers citing lack of knowledge about how to use it

alternative_due_to_internet_access.unit: percent of people choosing another payment method in some situations because of difficulty accessing the internet

mechanism.value: High stated preference does not eliminate capability barriers: knowledge, connectivity, speed, and context determine whether a preferred payment method is executable at the point of purchase

observations.method: BCB 2023 quantitative consumer survey of 1,500 individuals, with conditional barrier questions among Pix nonusers or people choosing alternatives.
observations.uncertainty: Preference and barrier shares use different conditional denominators; the release does not identify subgroup precision here or establish why internet access was difficult.
observations.subgroup: Brazilian consumers surveyed in 2023, with Pix users/nonusers and payment-choice contexts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Non-use may be intentional or situational, and reported knowledge barriers can coexist with access through family, merchants, or other payment rails.

denominator.unit: individuals in the BCB quantitative consumer survey; reported income-receipt measure compares the 2019 and 2023 editions

income_received_in_account_2019.unit: percent reporting receipt of their main income source into an account in 2019

income_received_in_account_2023.unit: percent reporting receipt of their main income source into an account in 2023

income_account_growth.unit: percentage-point increase from 2019 to 2023, calculated from published shares

merchant_pix_preference.unit: percent of surveyed establishments mentioning Pix among payment methods used or remembered

merchant_cash_presence.unit: percent of surveyed establishments mentioning cash

mechanism.value: Payment behavior is jointly produced by consumer receipt infrastructure and merchant acceptance: electronic income receipt expands the route into electronic payment, but cash remains materially present at the point of sale

observations.method: BCB comparison of the 2019 and 2023 consumer surveys plus a separate 2023 survey of 600 commercial establishments.
observations.uncertainty: Receipt into an account does not establish account usability, savings, income stability, or electronic-payment use; merchant mention is not transaction share or acceptance quality.
observations.subgroup: Brazilian consumers and surveyed commercial establishments in the BCB payment-habits study.
observations.counterinterpretation: Income may be received electronically but spent in cash, and merchant payment-method mentions can reflect availability rather than customer preference or actual volume.

related_sources.claim: BCB official publications portal listing the 2023 payment-habits study and microdata resources.
BCB official English release on Brazil’s 2024 Pix and card transaction growth, used as contextual continuation rather than the survey’s primary denominator.

boundary: This record adds a Brazil payment-diary, preference, merchant, and digital-barrier layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish causal Pix effects, financial welfare, merchant profitability, fraud reduction, cultural consumption, or universal cash displacement.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: BCB official 2023 payment-habits release reviewed for consumer, merchant, and diary sample sizes; cash/Pix diary shares, preference, non-use barriers, income receipt, and merchant mentions checked; official publication portal retained for underlying resources.
